skill.name: quality-gates
skill.description: Checkpoint framework and validation rules for coding agents that enforce quality gates across planning, implementation, testing, and review.
skill.summary: Enforces staged quality gates for agent-assisted software development.
skill.author: Barnhardt-Enterprises-Inc

security_audit.summary: Most static findings are false positives from Markdown examples, local API examples, secret-detection grep commands, and documentation links. One real risk remains: validate.py runs adjacent validator scripts through subprocess, so users must trust those scripts before execution. No prompt injection or data-exfiltration intent was found.

remediation.suggestion: Require explicit user confirmation before running validate.py, and show the exact validator scripts that will execute.
Pin, bundle, or checksum validator scripts before invoking them from .claude/skills paths.
Document that npm, npx, grep, and build commands should run only inside trusted repositories.
Label examples as non-executable documentation and keep dangerous examples clearly marked as violations.

content.value_statement: Validation often happens too late, after defects reach review. This skill gives Claude, Codex, and Claude Code staged quality gates for planning, testing, review, and release.
actual_capabilities: Defines pre-implementation, implementation, testing, and review gates for coding tasks.
Lists concrete TypeScript, security, testing, and build checks for each gate.
Provides validation rules for secrets, input validation, authorization, SQL safety, and Next.js patterns.
Documents TDD structure, coverage targets, and test quality expectations.
Includes a Python aggregator that runs installed validator scripts from adjacent skill folders.
limitations: The Python aggregator depends on other validator skills being installed in expected paths.
The examples focus on TypeScript, Next.js, Prisma, Jest, and Zod projects.
Shell commands must be reviewed before running inside untrusted repositories.
The skill does not prove business correctness without human review.

use_cases.title: Standardize Team Review Gates
use_cases.description: Apply the same planning, testing, security, and build checks across agent-assisted development work.

use_cases.title: Check Work Before Handoff
use_cases.description: Use staged gates to find missing tests, weak validation, or build failures before requesting review.

use_cases.title: Add Release Validation
use_cases.description: Run a final checklist that covers security, documentation, tests, build status, and known issues.

prompt_templates.title: Run Basic Gate Check
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner check for a current change
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the quality-gates skill to review my current change. Start with the implementation gate and list pass or fail items.

prompt_templates.title: Prepare Tests For A Feature
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the quality-gates testing gate for this feature. Identify required unit, integration, and UI tests before I finish the work.

prompt_templates.title: Audit Before Merge
prompt_templates.scenario: Review gate for a pull request
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the quality-gates review gate on this branch. Check security, tests, build status, documentation, and unresolved risks.

prompt_templates.title: Design Validation Workflow
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the quality-gates framework to design a repository validation workflow. Include gate order, required commands, manual checks, and exception handling.

output_examples.input: Review a small TypeScript API change before completion.
output: Implementation gate: TypeScript checks pass, but input validation is missing.
Testing gate: Add one invalid input test and one authenticated request test.
Review gate: Build and security review remain open.

output_examples.input: Prepare a final validation checklist for a feature branch.
output: Pre-implementation gate: Already satisfied by the approved plan.
Implementation gate: No hardcoded secrets or unsafe SQL patterns found.
Final gate: Run tests, build, and documentation checks before handoff.

output_examples.input: Assess whether a UI change has enough tests.
output: Testing gate: Unit coverage is acceptable for business logic.
UI gate: Add a DOM state assertion for the visual change.
E2E gate: Add one test for the user-visible workflow.

best_practices: Run gates early, then repeat them after tests and before final review.
Treat failed gates as work items, not as optional warnings.
Document approved exceptions with the reason and reviewer.
anti_patterns: Running every command automatically in an untrusted repository.
Using the checklist as a substitute for code review.
Skipping tests because the implementation appears small.

faq.question: What does this skill help with?
faq.answer: It gives coding agents a staged checklist for planning, implementation, testing, review, and final validation.

faq.question: Does it run commands automatically?
faq.answer: The documentation includes commands, and validate.py can run installed validator scripts when invoked.

faq.question: Which projects fit best?
faq.answer: It fits TypeScript, Next.js, Prisma, Jest, and Zod projects best, but the gate structure is adaptable.

faq.question: Can it replace a human reviewer?
faq.answer: No. It supports review discipline, but humans still need to judge product behavior and design tradeoffs.

faq.question: What should I check before running validators?
faq.answer: Review the repository, installed validator scripts, and command effects before running shell commands.

faq.question: Does it require other skills?
faq.answer: The checklist works alone, but validate.py expects several adjacent validator skills to be installed.
